text:
Washington led 2-1 after the second period's opening minutes on two snap shots that carried a combined 23 percent chance of going in, and that tells you how thin the Capitals' grip was. Boone Jenner's goal in the first and Justin Holl's in the second (8 percent) were the best Washington got from a night when Carolina out-attempted them 77 to 47. Washington did own the first period, 1.79 expected goals to 0.66, then produced 0.92 across the final two.

Carolina took the game over from there. Eric Robinson's snap shot (5 percent) tied it with 71 seconds left in the second, and the Hurricanes outchanced the Capitals 2.05 to 0.47 in the third. Andrei Svechnikov scored the power-play backhand at 13:56 to make it 3-2, then set up Mark Jankowski's backhand at 18:33, an 86 percent chance that made it 4-2. Svechnikov finished with two goals, an assist and five shots, and he and Sebastian Aho (two assists) both posted an expected-goals share near 2.8 against roughly 0.6 allowed.

Carolina deserved to win 60 percent of the time over simulated replays of every shot, and the 4.19 to 2.71 edge in total expected goals backs that up. Pyotr Kochetkov faced 22 shots, stopped all but two and beat the 2.71 expected against him. Logan Thompson allowed three on 3.33 expected, so he was fine; the Capitals were simply buried by volume, with 20 giveaways to Carolina's 12. This reverses the October 2 meeting, which Washington won 5-2 in Carolina.
